style.vernacular: Dense tropical capital of painted concrete: cream, white and grey rendered shophouses and townhouses of 3-5 storeys with roller shutters, signboards and rooftop water tanks; weathered mildew-stained concrete blocks with ribbon windows and balconies; glass-and-steel towers along the BTS and Sathorn/Sukhumvit corridors; and Buddhist temples (wat) with white walls, gilded ornament and stepped gable roofs of orange and green glazed tile. Traditional timber houses on stilts survive along canals. Flat concrete roofs are common on modern blocks; clay or glazed tile and corrugated metal on older and religious buildings.
style.ornament: Thai temple motifs: stepped chofa-tipped gable roofs in orange and green glazed tile, gilded naga bargeboards and finials, bell-shaped chedi spires, gold leaf and mirror-glass mosaic; spirit houses on pillars; shophouse roller shutters, hand-painted signboards and tangled overhead cables; rooftop water tanks and satellite dishes.

sources.what: traditional stilt houses, sala pavilions, Western and hybrid styles under Rama IV-VI, brick and laterite materials
mid-century modern Thai-influenced civic style with wide balconies for the tropical climate
